subject: Chemistry
title: Grignard Reagent: Why It Needs Dry Ether
summary: Alkyl halides react with magnesium in dry ether to give alkylmagnesium halides, RMgX: very useful, and destroyed by any trace of water. In this lesson: RX + Mg in dry ether gives RMgX (Victor Grignard, Nobel 1912), magnesium slipping between C and Br, the polar C-Mg bond with a carbanion-like carbon, the curved-arrow mechanism with water (RMgX + H2O → RH + Mg(OH)X), why moisture, alcohols and amines destroy it, and two solved questions.

notes.title: Grignard Reagent
notes.blurb: preparation, the c–mg bond, reaction with water (and other proton sources), solved questions

keyPoints: **Grignard reagent**: Alkyl **magnesium halide**. Victor Grignard: **Nobel Prize 1912**.
**The C–Mg bond**: Covalent but **very polar**. Carbon behaves like a **carbanion**.
**With water**: C–Mg pair takes **water's H**. Alcohols and amines do it too: **keep it dry**.

blocks.p: R–X + Mg —dry ether→ R–Mg–X · CH₃CH₂Br + Mg → CH₃CH₂MgBr (ethylmagnesium bromide)
Discovered by Victor Grignard (Nobel Prize in Chemistry, 1912). Magnesium inserts between the carbon and the halogen.

The C–Mg bond is covalent but highly polar: Mg is electropositive, so the bonding electrons are pulled towards carbon (Cδ−–Mgδ+). The carbon behaves like a carbanion (electron-rich, basic and nucleophilic). The Mg–X bond is essentially ionic.

sections.h: Reaction with water (and other proton sources)

blocks.p: **Mechanism:** the electron pair of the C–Mg bond attacks the H of water; the O–H electron pair goes to oxygen. The alkyl group leaves as the alkane R–H.
Water, alcohols, acids, and even amines are acidic enough to convert a Grignard reagent into a hydrocarbon. So it must be prepared and used in **dry ether**, with no moisture.

list: ✗ The C–Mg bond is ionic (it is polar covalent; Mg–X is ionic).
✗ The carbon of RMgX is δ+ (it is δ−).
✗ Grignard reagents can be made in aqueous solution (water destroys them).

blocks.p: **Q2.** Dry ether is needed because even traces of moisture convert RMgX into the alkane RH.

simulation.reason: The idea is a fixed sequence of steps drawn in the video and the notes; there is no continuous variable for a student to explore.

pyq.q: An organic compound (X) with molecular formula C₃H₆O is not readily oxidised. On reduction it gives C₃H₈O (Y), which reacts with HBr to give a bromide (Z), which is converted to a Grignard reagent. This Grignard reagent on reaction with (X) followed by hydrolysis gives 2,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol. Compounds (X), (Y) and (Z) respectively are:
pyq.explain: X = acetone (C₃H₆O, a ketone: not readily oxidised); Y = propan-2-ol (reduction); Z = 2-bromopropane; (CH₃)₂CHMgBr + acetone → after hydrolysis (CH₃)₂CH–C(OH)(CH₃)₂ = 2,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol.
